newsitem.title: ITALY: Benetton rises as analysts turn positive.
newsitem.headline: Benetton rises as analysts turn positive.

text.p: Shares in Italian clothing group Benetton showed a sharp rise on Tuesday as many analysts turned positive after a meeting with the company's management late last week following its first half 1996 results.
Broker Indosuez has changed its recommendation to buy from hold, justifying its decision by the net fall in the share price over previous weeks, while another broker Pasfin confirmed its buy stance.
The shares closed up 3.66 percent at 17,694 lire. They hit a year high in early July of 21,150 lire.

"We have changed the share's valuation for the reason of price, after the sharp fall of the last week and after the meeting on Friday with analysts that gave a positive message on the strength of the group's products," said Indosuez analyst Simone Concetti.

Pasfin analyst Elena Sottanella said it was possible to see by year's end a rise in net profits in the order of eight percent. This was after the group posted a rise of nine percent to 115.8 billion lire in first half net profits.
The group said that in terms of volume sales, the first six months of the year saw a three percent rise and by the end of the year that could be up four percent.
